arxiv-2109-11610.title: SPNet: Multi-Shell Kernel Convolution for Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2109-11610.creator: Yuyan Li, Chuanmao Fan *, Xu Wang *, Ye Duan
arxiv-2109-11610.description: Abstract Feature encoding is essential for point cloud analysis. In this paper, we propose a novel point convolution operator named Shell Point Convolution (SPConv) for shape encoding and local context learning. Specifically, SPConv splits 3D neighborhood space into shells, aggregates local features on manually designed kernel points, and performs convolution on the shells.

arxiv-2204-08197.title: Groups, drift and harmonic measures
arxiv-2204-08197.creator: Mark Pollicott and Polina Vytnova
arxiv-2204-08197.description: Abstract 1 Introduction An intriguing problem in modern geometric measure theory is the study of the harmonic measure on the unit circle which arises from a random walk on a Fuchsian group. The existing approach combines several areas of pure mathematics, such as Ergodic Theory, Probability Theory, Hyperbolic Geometry, and rigorous Numerical Analysis. We will first recall some background.

arxiv-2206-01754.description: Abstract Well-characterized binary systems will provide valuable opportunities to study the conditions that are necessary for the onset of both auroral and non-auroral magnetospheric radio emission in the ultracool dwarf regime. We present new detections of non-auroral “quiescent” radio emission at 4–8 GHz of the three ultracool dwarf binary systems GJ 564 BC, LP 415-20, and 2MASS J21402931+1625183.

arxiv-2309-10286.description: Abstract Efficiently counting or detecting defective items is a crucial task in various fields ranging from biological testing to quality control to streaming algorithms. The group testing estimation problem concerns estimating the number of defective elements d d in a collection of n n total within a given factor.

arxiv-2510-19582.title: From Interface Dynamics to Darcy Scale Description of Multiphase Flow in Porous Media Journal: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science
arxiv-2510-19582.creator: Steffen Berg, Ryan T. Armstrong, Maja Rücker, Alex Hansen, Signe Kjelstrup, Dick Bedeaux
arxiv-2510-19582.description: Abstract An outstanding characteristic of porous media, desired in many applications, is the large surface area, which facilitates solid-fluid interactions, making porous media an extreme case in colloid and interface science. In two-fluid systems, wetting and the balance of capillary and viscous forces control fluid displacement processes, leading to a wide range of complex flow regimes with rich spatio-temporal dynamics.

arxiv-2511-18544.title: Symbolic computation of optimal systems of subalgebras of three- and four-dimensional real Lie algebras
arxiv-2511-18544.creator: Luca Amata, Francesco Oliveri, Emanuele Sgroi
arxiv-2511-18544.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luca Amata, Francesco Oliveri, Emanuele Sgroi. The complete optimal systems of subalgebras of all nonisomorphic three- and four-dimensional real Lie algebras are analyzed by the program SymboLie running in the computer algebra system Wolfram Mathematica ™. The approach uses the definition of p p -families of Lie subalgebras whose set can be partitioned by introducing a binary relation (reflexive and transitive, though not necessarily symmetric) induced by inner automorphisms of the Lie algebra.

pmc-11612304.title: An Orai1 gain-of-function tubular aggregate myopathy mouse model phenocopies key features of the human disease
pmc-11612304.creator: Nan Zhao, Antonio Michelucci, Laura Pietrangelo, Sundeep Malik, Linda Groom, Jennifer Leigh, Thomas N O’Connor, Takahiro Takano, Paul D Kingsley, James Palis, Simona Boncompagni, Feliciano Protasi, Robert T Dirksen
pmc-11612304.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tubular aggregate myopathy (TAM) is a heritable myopathy primarily characterized by progressive muscle weakness, elevated levels of creatine kinase (CK), hypocalcemia, exercise intolerance, and the presence of tubular aggregates (TAs). Here, we generated a knock-in mouse model based on a human gain-of-function mutation which results in a severe, early-onset form of TAM, by inducing a glycine-to-serine point mutation in the ORAI1 pore (Orai1G100S/+ or GS mice).

pmc-11710370.title: Dissecting the mechanisms of CASK deficiency on the clearance of Aβ in microglia
pmc-11710370.creator: Jacky Chang, Yen Ting Cho, Yu Yi Lin, Irene Han‐Juo Cheng
pmc-11710370.description: BackgroundAmyloid‐beta (Aβ) deposition is a key pathological characteristic of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Microglia serves as a crucial system responsible for clearing Aβ. Activated microglia migrate towards Aβ deposits, engulf them, and breakdown Aβ through cathepsins within the lysosome. Calcium/calmodulin‐dependent serine protein kinase (CASK) regulates microglia’s migration and phagocytic activity.
